text: In 1932, Australia went to war against emus.
After World War One, veterans were given farms in Western Australia to grow wheat.
Then twenty thousand emus showed up, and ate it.
So the farmers called in the army.
Major Meredith arrived with two soldiers, two machine guns, and ten thousand bullets.
On the first day, the emus simply ran out of range.
Two days later, a thousand emus walked up to a dam, and the gun jammed.
So he bolted a gun onto a truck.
After a month, he claimed nine hundred and eighty-six emus, with nine thousand, eight hundred and sixty bullets.
Luckily, the army had plenty of bullets.
You see, a machine gun is made for an enemy that marches in a line.
Emus run fifty kilometres an hour, in every direction at once.
Meredith said an army that could take bullets like these birds could face any army in the world.
